title: U.S. House · Texas's 32nd District
area: A Dallas-area district covering parts of Dallas and Collin counties, including Richardson and Garland.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional map for the 2026 election cycle, and this is an open seat with no incumbent on the general-election ballot. Dan Barrios defeated Anthony Bridges in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 60.4% of the vote. The Republican primary runoff between Jace Yarbrough and Ryan Binkley was canceled, and Yarbrough advanced as the Republican nominee.

candidates.name: Dan Barrios
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 60.4% of the vote

summary.text: Dan Barrios is the Democratic nominee for the open 32nd District seat. He is a former business-sales account manager and high school business teacher who was elected to the Richardson City Council in 2023 and stepped down in September 2026 to focus on his congressional campaign. According to his Ballotpedia survey, he is running on education, affordable health care and support for small businesses.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia survey, he grew up in Brownsville, Texas, and has lived in North Texas for over 25 years.
Earned an MBA in strategic management from the University of North Texas.
Worked in executive sales and business development in the food and beverage industry, including as an account manager handling key accounts such as Walmart.
Taught business at Lake Highlands High School in the Richardson Independent School District; a May 2024 profile said he was finishing his fourth year of teaching.

Describes volunteer work with the American Red Cross, the Arapaho Classical Magnet PTA, the YMCA board and a church program serving people experiencing homelessness; he says he managed a shelter after the 2015 Rowlett tornado.
Sought the Richardson City Council Place 3 seat in 2019 and was elected to it in 2023, representing the city's District 3 on the west side of Richardson.
Announced on July 13, 2026 that he would resign from the council to focus on his congressional campaign; Daniel Burdette was appointed to the seat on September 28, 2026.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary over Anthony Bridges with 60.4% of the vote; his Ballotpedia survey lists endorsements from Rep. Julie Johnson and state Reps. Linda Garcia and Mihaela Plesa.

priorities.text: Supports investments in education and workforce development.
Says he backs policies that help small businesses grow and create local jobs.
Says he is committed to transparent, accountable government and expanding access to affordable, quality medical care.
priorities.quote: I am passionate about building transparent and accountable government that people can trust. I care deeply about education and ensuring every child has the opportunity to succeed, as well as expanding access to affordable, quality medical care.

positions.summary: Lists restoring access to reproductive healthcare, including codifying Roe v. Wade, among his congressional priorities.
positions.quote: Codify Roe v. Wade and protect access to contraception and IVF

positions.summary: Lists universal background checks and raising the age for certain semi-automatic rifles among his congressional priorities.
positions.quote: Require universal background checks, crack down on traffickers who illegally supply guns to criminals and street markets, and raise the age for certain semi-automatic rifles with high-capacity features.

positions.summary: Lists raising the corporate tax rate and closing tax loopholes among his congressional priorities.
positions.quote: Make billionaires and corporations pay their fair share, close loopholes like “buy, borrow, die” and “carried interest,” raise the corporate tax rate

positions.summary: Supports a federal public option and letting any American join Medicare.
positions.quote: Allow every American — regardless of age — to join Medicare: Provide an affordable, not-for-profit option that increases competition with private insurance and helps lower costs across the system.

positions.summary: Lists increasing the federal minimum wage among his congressional priorities.
positions.quote: Increase the federal minimum wage and expand overtime eligibility

positions.summary: Says he would reject private school voucher programs.
positions.quote: Reject private school voucher programs that divert taxpayer dollars away from neighborhood schools.

positions.summary: Says he would roll back tariff policies that raise costs for consumers and Texas businesses.
positions.quote: Roll back tariff policies that raise costs for American consumers and hurt Texas businesses.

positions.summary: Says he would stop offensive weapons sales to Israel while supporting defensive systems such as the Iron Dome.
positions.quote: Protect innocent life by stopping offensive weapons sales while supporting defensive systems like the Iron Dome.

statements.quote: Expand Early Childhood Education and Childcare: Establish universal Pre-K for every 3- and 4-year-old. Increase support for children under 3, protect Head Start programs, and make childcare more accessible and affordable.
statements.context: On the education section of his campaign issues page

statements.quote: Prevent corporate landlords and Wall Street investors from artificially inflating rents.
statements.context: On the taxes and affordability section of his campaign issues page

statements.quote: Expand construction and affordability programs, strengthen the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, reduce outdated regulatory barriers, and support modular housing to speed construction.
statements.context: On the taxes and affordability section of his campaign issues page

statements.quote: Support a mix of energy sources, streamline permitting for projects, invest in pipelines and supply chains for critical minerals, and restore federal incentives for renewable development.
statements.context: On the energy and environment section of his campaign issues page

statements.quote: Ensure agencies at the federal, state, and local levels have the resources to investigate and prosecute crime, while investing in training, oversight, and accountability for those who violate their oath.

statements.quote: Prioritize the deportation of criminals, gang members, and human traffickers — not neighbors who pay taxes and contribute to their communities.

candidates.name: Jace Yarbrough
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced as the Republican nominee after the scheduled May 26, 2026 primary runoff against Ryan Binkley was canceled

summary.text: Jace Yarbrough is the Republican nominee for the open 32nd District seat, a Dallas-based attorney and Air Force Reserve officer with degrees from the University of Texas at Austin and Stanford Law School. He ran for Texas State Senate District 30 in 2024, losing the Republican primary runoff, and was endorsed for this seat by President Trump. According to his Ballotpedia survey, he is running on border security, immigration enforcement and the America First agenda.

background.text: Raised in the Jim Ned area, a small West Texas community, according to a Dallas Express interview.
Earned a B.S. in electrical engineering and a B.A. in government from the University of Texas at Austin.
Served as an officer in the U.S. Air Force after graduating and continues in the Reserves, according to a January 2026 interview.
Attended Stanford Law School from 2015 to 2018 and became a Dallas-based trial attorney; Ballotpedia News describes him as a constitutional law attorney and co-founder of Saint Francis Academy.
In a 2023 interview he said he refused an order from his reserve command to take the COVID-19 vaccine, citing his faith, after 12 years of service.

Filed a federal lawsuit in October 2023 over a letter of admonishment he received for remarks at a 2021 military retirement ceremony; a judge allowed the case to proceed in September 2025. According to his Ballotpedia survey, First Liberty Institute represented him, and he says he served as an election-integrity lawyer for Donald Trump's campaign.
Ran for Texas State Senate District 30 in 2024, finishing second in the Republican primary on March 5 and losing the May 28 runoff to Brent Hagenbuch, 56.7% to 43.3%.

Advanced as the Republican nominee for the 32nd District after finishing in the top two of the March 3, 2026 primary and the May 26 runoff against Ryan Binkley was canceled; President Trump endorsed him on February 4, 2026.

priorities.text: Supports finishing a wall on the U.S.-Mexico border and ending "catch-and-release" immigration policy.
Supports tax cuts, expanded domestic energy production, and reduced federal spending.
Opposes U.S. military involvement in foreign conflicts he says do not directly threaten the United States, describing his position as "peace through strength."
priorities.quote: We must prioritize defending America—not foreign borders while ours remains wide open. I support peace through strength: a powerful military that deters aggression without deploying into unnecessary wars.

positions.summary: Supports finishing a border wall and ending "catch-and-release," and says he opposes abuse of visa and immigration programs.
positions.quote: President Trump needs reinforcements who will finish the wall, end catch-and-release, and stop illegal immigration threatening our workers and communities.

positions.summary: Says he will champion national concealed-carry reciprocity and a repeal of the National Firearms Act.
positions.quote: Jace Yarbrough will champion national reciprocity on concealed carry permits so law-abiding gun owners can lawfully carry when traveling over state lines, and a repeal of the National Firearms Act

positions.summary: Says he sued over implementation of Green New Deal policies and will continue to oppose them in Congress.
positions.quote: he sued the radical left over implementation of their job-crushing Green New Deal policies and will continue to fight them in Congress as he has done in court

researchNotes: This is an open seat under Texas's 2026 congressional map. Positions and statements for Dan Barrios come from the issue pages of his campaign website (each page read in a headless browser) and his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Jace Yarbrough's positions rely on his Ballotpedia survey and campaign site. No campaign-site statement on transgender athletes, voter citizenship proof or war powers was found for Barrios. Biography notes: the Texas State Senate runoff and 2024 primary figures come from Yarbrough's Ballotpedia page; no official campaign website was found for either candidate.
